subject: electric ray
title: Roman Doctors Prescribed a Live Electric Fish for Headaches

scenes.text: Roman doctors treated headaches with a live fish.
Around the year 47, the emperor's physician wrote it down: for a headache, hold a live torpedo ray to the forehead until it goes numb.
The fish was an electric ray. A big Atlantic torpedo grows six feet long and delivers up to 220 volts.
It hunts by wrapping its fins around a fish and shocking it.
Nobody would understand electricity for many centuries. And the naval weapon? Named after the fish.

description:
In the first century, Scribonius Largus, physician to the Roman emperor Claudius, prescribed a live electric ray as a painkiller.
In his book of remedies, published around AD 47, a live torpedo was to be placed on the forehead for a stubborn headache and under the feet for gout, and taken away once the spot went numb. The largest species, the Atlantic torpedo, reaches 1.8 meters and 90 kilograms and can deliver 170 to 220 volts, which it uses to stun fish it has wrapped in its fins and to defend itself. The naval torpedo was later named after the fish.
Would you have tried it? Comment below.

first_comment: The great doctor Galen tried the headache cure a century later and wrote that it did not work for him. Would you have let them put the fish on your head?
